title: Adequate moduli spaces are universal for separated targets
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $k$, and let $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. Assume, as in Alper’s Section 2 conventions, that the diagonals of $\mathcal X$ and $Y$ over $k$ are quasi-compact and separated: each scheme test of the absolute diagonal of $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic space with quasi-compact separated projection to the test scheme, and the diagonal of $Y$ is quasi-compact (its separatedness is automatic because it is a representable monomorphism). Scheme tests and relative diagonals use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-sfb-dm-stack-morphism-properties], the structural morphism to the base is [def-sfb-relative-moduli-inertia], and quasi-compactness and separatedness of the resulting space-to-scheme maps are [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli]. For every $k$-scheme $T$, and for every algebraic space $T/k$ whose diagonal is a closed immersion, composition with $\phi$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Mor}_k(Y,T)\simeq\operatorname{Mor}_k(\mathcal X,T)$. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]; maps out of a stack are taken up to 2-isomorphism, and their targets have only identity automorphisms. There is no assertion here for arbitrary nonseparated algebraic spaces.

source.place: Theorem 7.2.1, printed pp.36--37: locally separated targets or targets Zariski-locally with affine diagonal. The stated cases are schemes and separated algebraic spaces. Read arXiv:1005.2398v3 online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Use the explicit quasi-compact separated absolute diagonal assumptions, which are the standing convention of Alper Section 2. First treat any algebraic space $T/k$ whose diagonal is an immersion. By [lem-sfb-adequate-geometric-fibres-submersion], $\phi$ is universally submersive and two $\Omega$-objects over the same point of $Y(\Omega)$ have intersecting closures in $|\mathcal X_\Omega|$, for every algebraically closed $\Omega/k$. By [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], $\phi$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $\mathcal O_Y\simeq\phi_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$. These are exactly the hypotheses on $p$ in [lem-sfb-stein-submersive-reduced-descent]; no noetherian or finite-type hypothesis is being introduced.

source.place: Theorem 7.2.1 locally separated case; Proposition 7.1.1 conditions (a)--(c).

proof.text: Fix $h:\mathcal X\to T$ and put $R=(\mathcal X\times_Y\mathcal X)_{\mathrm{red}}$ with projections $p_1,p_2$. An algebraically closed point $r$ of $R$ gives two objects $x_1,x_2$ with $\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2)$. Their closures intersect by [lem-sfb-adequate-geometric-fibres-submersion], and [lem-sfb-locally-separated-closure-equivalent-images] gives $h(x_1)=h(x_2)$ as points of $T(\Omega)$, not just equality of their underlying topological images. This holds over every algebraically closed extension.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.1 proof: condition (a) implies surjectivity of W.

proof.text: Form the actual fibre product $W=R\times_{(hp_1,hp_2),\,T\times_kT,\,\Delta_T}T$. In a local closed/open factorization of $\Delta_T$, pullback restricts the open subspace and pulls back the defining ideal; hence $W\to R$ is an immersion. Step 2 makes it surjective on geometric points. On each reduced smooth scheme chart of $R$, choose open neighbourhoods where the immersion is closed. On each neighbourhood its ideal has full vanishing locus, so every element lies in every prime, is nilpotent, and is zero by reducedness. Thus the immersion is an isomorphism on the chart and therefore on $R$. The defining universal property of $W$ now gives $hp_1=hp_2$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.1 proof, final cartesian diagram: a surjective immersion into the reduced relation is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stein-submersive-reduced-descent] with $p=\phi$, using the hypotheses checked in step 1 and $hp_1=hp_2$ from step 3. It supplies a morphism $g:Y\to T$ with $g\phi=h$, and injectivity makes it unique. Consequently precomposition is bijective for every target with immersive diagonal.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.1 proof, exact Hom diagram; Theorem 7.2.1 locally separated case.

proof.text: For a $k$-scheme $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-diagonal-immersion] applied to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives an immersive diagonal, so step 4 applies even when $T$ is nonseparated. For an algebraic space whose diagonal is a closed immersion, that diagonal is an immersion by its defining local factorization, using the whole target as the open subspace; step 4 applies again. The morphisms throughout were over $k$, so these are the two required bijections of $k$-morphisms.

lean.statement: theorem adequateModuliSpace_universal_schemes_separatedSpaces {k : Type u} [Field k] (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (Y : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (φ : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli Y.obj.obj)) (hφ : IsAdequateModuliSpace F hF Y φ) (hFdiag : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct (moduliBaseStructure F) (moduliBaseStructure F))), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange (moduliRelativeDiagonal (moduliBaseStructure F)) T t Z p ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact p ∧ MapToSchemeIsSeparated Z T p) (hYdiag : MapIsQuasiCompact (prod.lift (𝟙 Y.obj.obj) (𝟙 Y.obj.obj))) : (∀ (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (h : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T))), ∃! g : Y.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T, Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (φ.comp (discreteModuliMap g)) h)) ∧ (∀ (T : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 T.obj.obj) (𝟙 T.obj.obj)) → ∀ (h : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli T.obj.obj)), ∃! g : Y.obj.obj ⟶ T.obj.obj, Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (φ.comp (discreteModuliMap g)) h))
lean.note: Unique factorization with Nonempty ModuliTwoIso is the bijection on 2-isomorphism classes; the targets are discrete fibred groupoids. The two conjuncts keep arbitrary scheme targets and closed-diagonal algebraic spaces separate. Source Section 2 diagonal convention is explicit in statement_change.
